title: Why plane windows have no corners
pause_note: Channel v5, first 'Why Is It Designed Like That?' Short. DO + STAKE hook: count the corners at 0 s (a square window morphing round); stake (1954 Comet) at ~4 s; reveal (stress piles up at a corner) at ~9 s; crack grows; fix; loop; one-word question.

beats: Next time you fly, count the corners on your window. There are none.
In 1954, the first jet airliner kept breaking up in midair.
Every flight pumps the cabin up like a balloon, then lets it down.
Around a sharp corner, all that stretch piles up in one tiny spot.
Flight after flight, a crack grew from one square corner, until the cabin burst.
Round the corners, and the stress flows smoothly around the hole.
